subject: How can i identify anchor items in a bifactor model without prior  knowledge？

messages.author: 23324484cf9b05bb
messages.subject: How can i identify anchor items in a bifactor model without prior  knowledge？
parts:
Hello  everyone ：）
I am using mirt package in r studio to fit a bifactor model.
code like this：

fstruct2=c(2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,3,3,3,3)

mod2=bfactor(irt[,1:12],fstruct2,iterations=1000)

However，when i tried to test DIF between male and female，i did not know which items should be identify as anchor items.(If there is no anchor items, DIF test will be DIF+latent trait distribution)

SO i would like to ask, how can i identify anchor items in a bifactor model without prior  knowledge？

I have read <<Anchor Selection Strategies for DIF Analysis: Review, Assessment, and New Approaches>> by Kopf et.al(2015), but there is no specific code：（

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: How can i identify anchor items in a bifactor model without prior knowledge？
parts:
Anchor selection is generally a theoretical question, so you'd have to think of  the underlying causal mechanisms that should be considered (approximately) equivalent across across groups. Kopf provides statistical approaches to identifying anchors, which has some use of course for exploratory purposes, but at the end of the day the decision on what should be kept as invariant must be scientifically justifiable. I also haven't implemented any of the anchor search strategies myself, though perhaps one day I'll play around with this idea in the package.

Phil
